title: Mayfly queue job envelope
description: The JSON body of one queue job. A producer writes this body to a queue backend, and a worker decodes it before running the job. The version is a major version: a change that removes, renames, or retypes a field, or changes what an existing field means, increments it. Optional fields may be added without a new version, so a reader ignores fields it does not know. A reader that does not know a major version, or a kind, buries the job with a reason instead of running it.

kind.description: The work a worker does. session.create creates one session from the prompt and options. source.run runs one scheduled data source and creates a session only when the run has changes the schedule triggers on.

id.description: Job id. Mayfly assigns it when the job is admitted. A producer may omit it; the queue derives one from the idempotency key, or generates one when there is no key. The id names the job in GET /api/v1/queue/jobs/{id} and in the session trigger.

idempotency_key.description: The producer's deduplication key. The same key with the same kind and trigger name is accepted once and answers as a duplicate until queue.dedupe_ttl expires. Without a key every message is a new job.

created_at.description: When the producer created or the queue accepted the job, in UTC.

attempts.description: How many times a worker has failed to finish the job. Mayfly maintains this field; a producer omits it.

agent.description: Agent name for the session. Empty selects the default agent.

prompt.description: The first user message of the session. Required for session.create.

session.description: Session options other than the prompt and agent.

source.description: The scheduled run to execute. Required for source.run.

metadata.description: Producer labels carried with the job. Mayfly does not interpret them. A reader keeps fields it does not know.

kind.description: What caused the job, such as github, slack, datadog, generic, schedule, or api.

event.description: Event within the trigger, such as pull_request or webhook.

actor.description: Person or account that caused the event, when the producer knows it.

title.description: Session title. Empty uses the first line of the prompt.

model.description: Model name. It must be the default model or an entry of llm.allow_models.

ttl.description: Session lifetime as a Go duration such as 30m or 1h30m. Empty uses the configured default.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers the session may call.

artifacts.description: Inputs the producer already stored. The session may read them; the control plane only checks the reference.

key.description: Object-store key, relative to the artifact store.

sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the stored bytes.

content_type.description: Media type of the stored bytes.

run_id.description: Run id written into the run artifact. Defaults to the job id.

schedule.description: Schedule name from the compiled bundle.

source.description: Data source name the schedule reads.

slot.description: Cron slot this run covers, in UTC.
